proposed_from.topic: Graphwise completeness of latent subpopulation S-ID on native-forest traces. For every finite childless-selector augmented ADMG G^S and disjoint X,Y satisfying NativeForestTrace(G^S;X,Y)—the initial selected d-separation check passes and every reachable terminal S-Hedge admits nested common-root forests whose directed and bidirected edges are actual edges of G^S[N_S]—work over the full positive recursive augmented-SCM class whose declared observed-parent interfaces and shared-exogenous incidences induce exactly G^S. Prove that Abouei et al.'s Algorithm 1 succeeds if and only if P(Y | do(X=x), S=1) is graphwise identifiable from P(V | S=1) over all finite signatures, comparing models only within one signature. On success return the published Eq. 23 functional. On terminal native failure construct one finite multistate exact-graph counterpair with the same strictly positive selected law and unequal intervention-before-conditioning targets, using a positive ordinary-forest separator, common full-support randomized-response routing along actual treatment-avoiding paths, and inert finite-state exactification. Prove explicit graph-recursion bounds and sound finite checking of any supplied rational certificate; do not claim a binary, rational, or executable failure constructor. Preserve unrestricted virtual-edge graphwise completeness, the positive-binary two-virtual-edge separator, the initial selected-d-separation failure construction, exact-rational inverse lifting, and total success-or-certificate compilation as open questions. Retain the UK Biobank component only as a conditional two-selector feasibility audit.
proposed_from.novelty_justification: The proposal turns Abouei et al.'s sufficient latent S-ID algorithm into an exact graphwise criterion on their own induced-graph class, rather than on a nonminimal supergraph class. Each SCM has declared parent interfaces equal to \(\operatorname{Pa}_{G^S}\), and shared-exogenous incidence agrees exactly with the bidirected edge set. Every terminal failure constructs a typed projected hedge record with Shpitser--Pearl incidence conditions, equal positive projected observational kernels, and a named local \(D_i=C\) contrast; a separate bridge proves that this contrast survives Eq. 23 placement. The resulting pair is compiled into rational finite-binary certificates, and exactification preserves every selected atom and intervention-before-conditioning target while restoring exact graph equality. The checker validates exact graph equality, normalized selected-law equality, and target separation. Unlike ordinary hedge completeness, the inverse construction must jointly realize virtual bidirected edges sharing or branching through selection ancestors. Chen et al. provide only a forward conditioning transformation, Kivva et al. provide positive finite separators for a different conditional-identification input, and Lee, Ghassami, and Shpitser use multiple systematic-selection regime distributions rather than one selected law and do not supply the exact-graph same-law inverse lift. The exact two-virtual-edge fiber separation is load-bearing, after which the effective arbitrary shared-ancestor lift remains the first-class open question.

seed_details.kernel: Prove that latent S-ID Algorithm 1 succeeds if and only if \(P_X(Y\mid S=1)\) is graphwise identified, returning Eq. 23 or a positive finite-binary counterpair.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the ordinary hedge countermodel step by an inverse lift that preserves the entire normalized selected law through all ancestors of \(S\).
seed_details.destination_search: Searches of latent S-ID, selected SCM conditioning, systematic selection, 2026 selection-bias identification, and positive conditional identification found no proof of the conjectured converse or failure-pair compiler.
seed_details.opened_evidence: The anchor's Introduction motivates latent S-components as the missing extension; Theorem 5.1 and Algorithm 1 prove soundness and give Eq. 23; the recursive proof stops at the S-Hedge failure case; the Conclusion explicitly leaves completeness open.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: ordinary hedge completeness applies after suppressing selection ancestors. Rebuttal: suppression creates virtual bidirected edges with shared structural equations, and ordinary counterpairs do not preserve one normalized \(P(V\mid S=1)\) under inverse realization.
seed_details.burned_reason: Angle 0 exhausted six revisions on universal positive selected-law inverse lifting and exact certificate compilation before the NativeForestTrace pivot.

seed_details.kernel: Construct an inverse-lift theorem for every projected ordinary hedge pair through arbitrarily shared and branching ancestors of \(S\), preserving strict selected-law equality and the target gap.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Assemble all virtual-edge realizations into one parameter fiber before perturbing any latent or selection mechanism.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches found forward SCM conditioning and commutation results, ordinary latent projection, and single-district lifts, but no counterpair inverse realization across overlapping ancestor paths.
seed_details.opened_evidence: Abouei's S-component definition locates the virtual connectivity; Chen's Theorem on conditioned SCM semantics controls conditioning, marginalization, and intervention in the forward direction and explicitly limits intervention commutation to variables outside selection ancestors.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: lift each virtual edge independently with an XOR chain. Rebuttal: overlapping paths reuse ancestor equations and the same selection normalizer, so edgewise lifts can destroy full selected-law equality.

seed_details.kernel: Characterize the finite-binary sharp range of \(P_X(Y\mid S=1)\) from a fixed positive selected law and prove universal singleton collapse if and only if Algorithm 1 succeeds.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Encode equality to the normalized selected law with an unknown positive selection normalizer while retaining intervention-before-conditioning target polynomials.
seed_details.destination_search: AutoBounds covers discrete selection problems generically, but no S-Hedge-indexed endpoint formula or equivalence between universal singleton collapse and latent S-ID success was located.
seed_details.opened_evidence: Duarte et al.'s Introduction frames sharp bounds as the output after point-ID failure; Theorem 1 proves equivalence of canonical response-function optimization and sharp bounds; its selection simulations do not analyze S-Hedges or graphwise singleton collapse.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: this is an immediate AutoBounds instance. Rebuttal: the polynomial program is available, but the graphwise singleton frontier and any analytic primitive-S-Hedge endpoints are not consequences stated or proved there.

seed_details.kernel: Give a direct binary response-function construction producing a strictly positive same-selected-law separator for every S-Hedge without passing through a projection theorem.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the ordinary parity cancellation by a global nullspace perturbation over selected atomic probabilities and require a nonzero selected interventional contrast.
seed_details.destination_search: The ordinary binary hedge construction and Kivva et al.'s positive multivalued perturbation were found; neither is a universal positive binary S-Hedge construction.
seed_details.opened_evidence: Shpitser and Pearl's C-forest proof uses binary parity models and sketches a positivity modification; Kivva et al. instead use an odd-cardinality positive perturbation orthogonal to observational kernel vectors.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: positivity follows by adding independent bit noise to the ordinary hedge pair. Rebuttal: convolution can erase the selected target contrast, and conditioning renormalizes the two models differently unless equality is imposed jointly.

seed_details.kernel: Prove completeness when the incidence hypergraph of virtual bidirected-edge paths through \(A_S\) is a forest, and characterize the first branching obstruction.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Order ancestor-chain gadgets leaf-to-root so each telescoping equality introduces one unused latent bit.
seed_details.destination_search: No selected-SCM or latent-projection result located a tree-incidence boundary for inverse countermodel realization.
seed_details.opened_evidence: Chen's intervention-conditioning commutation proof isolates ancestor dependence, while Abouei's recursion identifies exactly which S-components require the construction.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: a forest restriction is an arbitrary subclass. Rebuttal: it is the maximal class supported by edge-elimination without shared-cycle constraints and becomes the principled pivot if the branching kill test fails.

seed_details.kernel: Decide the exact selected-law fiber for \(G_\star^S\) and \(Q_\star\), returning a symbolic pair or a proof of fiber constancy.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Write all binary selected atoms and target numerators as polynomials in response-type probabilities before normalizing.
seed_details.destination_search: No paper analyzes this graph; general polynomial bounds can decide it computationally but do not expose the compositional obstruction.
seed_details.opened_evidence: The anchor's terminal S-Hedge case supplies the graph-theoretic failure, but its proof gives neither a pair nor a selected-law fiber calculation.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: one six-node graph is a hand-tuned witness. Rebuttal: the objection caps the result at subfield, but the graph is the minimal branching gate whose answer determines whether the flagship kernel is coherent.

seed_details.kernel: For a declared successful Eq. 23 graph class, derive the efficient influence function and an attaining cross-fitted estimator under selected-law sampling.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Differentiate the selected S-component kernels and project the resulting score onto the tangent space induced by their normalized equality constraints.
seed_details.destination_search: Ordinary ADMG influence-function and primal-fixable estimators exist, but no selected-law Eq. 23 efficiency result was found.
seed_details.opened_evidence: Bhattacharya, Nabi, and Shpitser derive primal and dual weights, influence functions, and efficient projections for ordinary ADMG classes; their Conclusion leaves general identified effects open. Abouei et al. provide identification but no estimation theory.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: apply the functional delta method to Eq. 23. Rebuttal: selected normalization and equality constraints inherited through \(A_S\) alter both the derivative and the efficient tangent-space projection.

seed_details.kernel: Show that every latent S-ID failure has nonidentification on a relatively open region of strictly positive selected laws, rather than only at one countermodel pair.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Turn a same-law target-separating pair into a rank-stable fiber direction under perturbations of selected atomic probabilities.
seed_details.destination_search: Ordinary graphwise completeness needs only one pair and the selected-law literature does not state a generic-fiber separation theorem.
seed_details.opened_evidence: The ordinary hedge proof constructs a point witness, while the latent S-ID paper conjectures graphwise nonidentification but makes no robustness claim across observed laws.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: graphwise nonidentification requires only one law, so genericity is cosmetic. Rebuttal: a relatively open failure region distinguishes structural ambiguity from a measure-zero parity coincidence and supports stable partial-identification diagnostics.

seed_details.kernel: State an augmented graph for UK Biobank recruitment, eligibility, and imaging follow-up, then return an identifying functional or an S-Hedge pair for the exact HbA1c selected-subpopulation target.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the usual population MR independence assertion by independence after each documented selection event and keep the two sample laws distinct.
seed_details.destination_search: Participation, imaging, and MR-bias studies document the selectors, but no paper applies latent S-ID to this target or states a unified augmented graph.
seed_details.opened_evidence: Tian et al.'s Introduction and Methods define the clinical target, two nonoverlapping samples, and exclusions; the Discussion notes healthy-volunteer and ancestry limits. Tyrrell, Lyall, and Schoeler document genetic, cardiometabolic, cognitive, and socioeconomic predictors of participation and imaging.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: the graph is analyst-chosen and the result is a case study. Rebuttal: the audit is useful only as a consumer of a general certificate theorem, so it is retained as an application proposition rather than the kernel.

seed_details.kernel: Characterize when latent S-ID is ordinary ID in the conditioned SCM and derive the boundary where intervention and conditioning cease to commute.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Apply ordinary ID after the conditioned-SCM transformation and compare the result with intervention before selection conditioning.
seed_details.destination_search: The anchor already proves causal-semantic preservation and the exact commutation condition for interventions outside selection ancestors.
seed_details.opened_evidence: Chen, Zoeter, and Mooij's central theorem and intervention corollary already establish the proposed reduction when the treatment is outside \(\operatorname{An}(S)\), and give counterexamples inside it.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: this is immediate from ChenZoeterMooij2024 plus ordinary ID. The objection holds; the seed is dropped.
